articles.title: David Gilliver: I'm a British photography award winner – I might need to quit next year
articles.summary: David Gilliver is a mainstay at the British Photography Awards, but his future in the industry isn't certain
articles.body:
Award-winning photographer David Gilliver has built an international reputation from his playful miniature worlds, secured global commercial clients and collected some of the industry's most prestigious prizes.

Despite being nominated in four categories at this year's British Photography Awards - winning one of them - the 47-year-old fears he may not be able to sustain a career behind the camera.

He said if 2027 is like 2026, he may have to find a part-time job.

His fears highlight the pressures facing even established artists, as consumers cut discretionary spending and art sales fall.

Gilliver has been a mainstay at the British Photography Awards since the Covid-19 pandemic when his depiction of miniature swimmers on the pool-like lines of a medical mask impressed the judging panel.

His latest nominations come after more than three decades behind the camera.

His roots in professional photography go back to the late 1990s when he enrolled in a fine art photography degree at Glasgow's School of Art.

It was during this time when he developed a passion for macro photography, a style using perspective to create amusing and striking images.

His individual take on it involves miniature figurines, his "little people", positioned against true-to-size objects to create juxtaposed scenes.

But after struggling to find sustained work, he "took the plunge" to find more stable employment and headed to the Channel Islands, where his sister lived.

In 2001, he moved to Guernsey and found a role in the finance industry.

"It was meant to last six months, but that turned into 14 years," he said.

Though a more lucrative avenue at the time, the day job couldn't entirely overshadow his creative work.

"My art practice [was] very much alive in the background," he said.

"It was during my time on Guernsey that I became interested in light painting and night photography.

"I started going out at night time and discovering the island under the cover of darkness, which no-one else seemed to be doing at the time, and documented Guernsey in a very unique manner."

This was flipped on its head in 2012 when he herniated a disc in his spine while "swinging kettlebells around" at a fitness class.

"It completely wrecked my lower back," he said.

"I was in absolute agony. I could barely sit down."

After years of surgery, physio appointments and several attempts to return to the office, he decided the pain was unbearable and he was forced into a life-changing decision – to drop the career and make photography pay while also raising a young daughter.

"I just quite simply had to make it work," he said.

Over the next decade he hustled and honed his craft with a focus on the "little people" series and light photography in order to position himself in two niche areas of the art in a bid to make a living from it.

In four of the last five years, he has won accolades at the British Photography Awards, being nominated in four categories at the 2026 ceremony.

The competition now welcomes more than 40,000 entrants each year, with just 40 people receiving awards at the annual gala in central London's Royal Lancaster hotel.

"When I was shortlisted for four this year, I was quite speechless actually, because normally it's just one or two images that you manage to sneak in," he said.

A shoot with an international car company won the commercial award this year, but another highlight was being nominated in the food and drink category with an absurdist scene of miniature firefighters extracting juice from grapes to refill their wine bottle.

"I mean, it's just ridiculous," he said.

"I had the cheek to enter that into the food and drink category alongside professional food photographers."

This child-like playfulness has been part of why his style has been so successful, with Gilliver saying despite his years in the profession, his work is still only 10% technique and camera skills, and 90% creativity.

"The strength of the work lies in the concepts and the silly ideas," he said.

His unique style also often prompts others to ask "What goes on inside your head?", the title of his entry in this year's self-portrait category.

It shows his little figurines playing, working and dancing around his head.

But despite the awards, the industry is still tough in the current economic climate, Gilliver said.

As people feel squeezed by inflation, he said he has to keep "extremely busy" to fill his schedule, doing everything from teaching workshops to writing books.

"The problem with years like this year where it's a very nervous economy and people aren't spending as much, one of the first things people stop doing is buying art and that has been very evident," he said.

"I mean, I'm probably over 60%, 70% down in terms of art sales, which is quite concerning.

"My monthly workshops, they are probably at least 50% down as well."

The awards have helped him to secure several commercial shoots with companies able to pay a larger sum than the average art buyer, but he isn't entirely sure what lies ahead.

"Things feel like they're going well on paper, and there's not much further elbow room in terms of general improvement," he said.

"I think that's where things are a little bit worrying."

Despite this, he is determined to carry on.

"I'm going to squeak by this year, I think, just."

Another big commercial shoot is on the horizon and he hopes it could put 2027 on more stable footing.

But unlike other artists who eventually quit to find a more stable profession behind a desk, Gilliver said his health leaves him with few alternatives.

"If I don't make this work, I have nothing else to really fall back on," he said.

articles.title: Carro pega fogo e interdita faixa da Rodovia Anhanguera em Campinas | G1
articles.standfirst: Uma faixa e o acostamento foram interditados no km 95 para atendimento da ocorrência.
articles.summary: Incêndio atingiu um carro no km 95 da Rodovia Anhanguera, em Campinas. Ninguém ficou ferido e não houve congestionamento no trecho.
articles.body:
Um carro pegou fogo no início da tarde deste sábado (14), na Rodovia Anhanguera (SP-330), em Campinas (SP). A ocorrência foi registrada no sentido sul, na altura do km 95. Ninguém ficou ferido.

Segundo a AutoBAn, concessionária responsável pelo trecho, o veículo estava parado no acostamento quando o incêndio começou.

Por segurança, uma faixa da pista e o acostamento precisaram ser interditados durante o atendimento da ocorrência. Apesar da interdição, não houve registro de congestionamento no trecho.

Carro pega fogo e faixas são interditadas na Rodovia Anhanguera, em Campinas — Foto: Andrey Correa

Um incêndio em vegetação foi registrado na Rua Armando Pinareli, ao lado do Condomínio Residencial Sírius, em Campinas por volta do meio-dia deste sábado (14).

A fumaça chamou atenção de moradores, que registraram imagens do local.

O Corpo de Bombeiros fez o combate às chamas e o rescaldo na área afetada. Não houve registro de feridos.

Incêndio atinge área de vegetação em Campinas — Foto: Wilson Alves Cruz Junior/Reprodução EPTV

articles.title: Chuvas intensas no Ceará: Funceme emite alerta para 42 cidades | G1
articles.standfirst: Há possibilidade de chuvas moderadas a fortes, descargas elétricas e rajadas de vento. O alerta vale do fim da noite deste sábado (14) até a madrugada de domingo (15).
articles.summary: Chuvas intensas no Ceará podem atingir o Cariri e Sertão Central com raios e ventos fortes; veja a lista das 42 cidades em alerta pela Funceme até segunda-feira.
articles.body:
A Fundação Cearense de Meteorologia e Recursos Hídricos (Funceme) emitiu um aviso meteorológico para 42 cidades do Ceará devido ao risco de chuvas intensas . Entre os municípios incluídos está Crato , onde uma tempestade registrada na noite da última segunda-feira (9) causou transtornos.

Segundo a Funceme, o aviso é válido entre o fim da noite deste sábado (14) e a madrugada de domingo (15), com possibilidade de novos episódios entre a noite de domingo (15) e a madrugada de segunda-feira (16).

O documento técnico aponta risco potencial para ocorrência de chuvas intensas, com probabilidade entre 20% e 40% . As regiões do Cariri e do Sertão Central e Inhamuns concentram os municípios incluídos na área de atenção.

Segundo a Funceme, o cenário está associado à atuação de um cavado em altos níveis da atmosfera. “A evolução e o deslocamento desse sistema em direção ao norte do Nordeste brasileiro poderão favorecer o aumento da instabilidade atmosférica sobre o centro-sul do Ceará”, informou o órgão.

A fundação destacou ainda que não estão descartados episódios de chuva de intensidade moderada a forte, acompanhados de rajadas de vento e descargas elétricas. Durante a madrugada de domingo, os ventos podem atingir até 40 km/h.

Fortaleza não está na lista da Funceme. — Foto: Thiago Gadelha/SVM

articles.title: Motorista foge pelado após acidente com caminhonete em Jataí | G1
articles.standfirst: Condutor perdeu o controle da caminhonete, destruiu palmeiras em avenida de Jataí e foi embora a pé. Órgão de trânsito informou que ele já foi identificado pela placa do veículo.
articles.summary: Motorista foge pelado em Jataí após bater caminhonete e destruir palmeiras; identificado pela placa, ele responderá por crime de dano ao patrimônio público.
articles.body:
O motorista de uma caminhonete fugiu pelado depois de causar um acidente em Jataí , no sudoeste do estado. Câmeras de segurança registraram quando ele sai do veículo sem roupas (veja o vídeo acima) .

O nome do motorista não foi divulgado. Por isso, o g1 não conseguiu localizá-lo para que se posicionasse sobre o caso.

O acidente aconteceu na madrugada de sexta-feira (13). O vídeo mostra uma caminhonete preta trafegando por uma avenida de Jataí. Em seguida, o veículo sobe no canteiro central e derruba duas palmeiras.

Pouco depois, o motorista desce do veículo sem roupas. O homem ainda abre as outras portas da caminhonete e parece procurar alguma coisa. Segundo apuração da TV Anhanguera, após olhar dentro do veículo, o motorista saiu e deixou a caminhonete em cima do canteiro. Não há registro de feridos.

A Superintendência de Trânsito de Jataí informou que conseguiu identificar o motorista pela placa da caminhonete. O órgão de trânsito disse que ele deve responder pelo crime de dano ao patrimônio público e também precisará arcar com os prejuízos causados ao canteiro.

articles.title: Construção sustentável: técnicas reduzem calor e geram economia | G1
articles.standfirst: Em São José do Rio Preto, materiais como EPS e tijolos ecológicos ajudam a deixar imóveis mais frescos e reduzir o impacto ambiental. Já em Penápolis, uma iniciativa oferece oportunidade de trabalho e renda para mulheres em situação de vulnerabilidade social.
articles.summary: Com o uso de EPS e tijolos ecológicos, a construção sustentável garante conforto térmico, reduz custos e ainda gera renda para mulheres em situação de vulnerabilidade.
articles.body:
Com as ondas de calor cada vez mais frequentes e intensas, manter a casa em uma temperatura agradável deixou de ser apenas uma questão de conforto. O isolamento térmico dos imóveis também está relacionado à saúde, à qualidade de vida e ao consumo de energia elétrica.

Em busca de soluções para esse desafio, profissionais da construção civil têm investido em materiais e técnicas mais sustentáveis .

Construção civil investe em materiais sustentáveis em São José do Rio Preto — Foto: TV TEM/ Reprodução

Em São José do Rio Preto (SP), alternativas como o EPS, conhecido popularmente como isopor, e os tijolos ecológicos vêm ganhando espaço nos projetos. Além de contribuir para o conforto térmico dos ambientes, esses materiais podem reduzir o desperdício e diminuir a quantidade de resíduos gerados durante as obras.

Uma casa construída com placas de EPS na cidade é um exemplo dessa tecnologia. Depois de pronta, a diferença em relação a uma construção convencional praticamente não aparece. Isso porque o acabamento é feito com argamassa, assim como em outros imóveis.

O EPS pode ser utilizado de diferentes maneiras, dependendo do projeto e do sistema construtivo. Em determinadas situações, a tecnologia pode representar uma economia de até 30% no custo da obra.

Uma fábrica de Rio Preto trabalha com esse tipo de material desde a década de 1980. No processo de produção, as placas recebem uma malha de aço, que integra o sistema utilizado na construção.

O empresário Otávio de March acompanha a evolução do mercado e destaca o aumento da procura pelo material ao longo dos anos.

"Na época, a gente construía duas a três casas por ano com esse material. Hoje em dia, a gente chega a produzir até 30 casas por ano com esse tipo de material. Foi uma mudança no comportamento e no conhecimento das pessoas", conta.

Além do isolamento térmico, o sistema permite que as peças sejam produzidas nas medidas necessárias para cada projeto, facilitando a montagem e evitando desperdícios. As sobras também podem ser reaproveitadas, reduzindo o descarte de resíduos da construção civil no meio ambiente.

Outra alternativa utilizada por arquitetos são os tijolos ecológicos. Os furos presentes nas peças formam bolsões de ar, que contribuem para o desempenho termoacústico das construções. O sistema também pode diminuir a necessidade de ferragens, dependendo das características do projeto.

O arquiteto Marcelo Cury explica que a escolha dos materiais pode fazer diferença não apenas no conforto dos moradores, mas também na quantidade de resíduos produzidos durante a obra.

"Em um projeto recente, de uma casa com 218 metros quadrados, a previsão inicial era utilizar 60 caçambas para o descarte de resíduos da construção civil. Com a adoção de soluções sustentáveis, esse volume foi reduzido para apenas dez. É uma alvenaria pensada para melhorar a qualidade de vida e também ajudar o meio ambiente", explica o arquiteto.

O projeto também prioriza a circulação de ar e a entrada de iluminação natural. Com ambientes mais arejados e bem iluminados, a necessidade de utilizar ar-condicionado e lâmpadas durante o dia diminui, o que pode representar economia na conta de energia.

Uso de materiais sustentáveis ganha espaço na construção civil no interior de SP — Foto: TV TEM/ Reprodução

Sustentabilidade também gera renda para mulheres em Penápolis

A sustentabilidade também pode ser uma ferramenta de transformação social. Em Penápolis, na região de Araçatuba (SP), um projeto da autarquia municipal de água e esgoto une a conservação dos espaços públicos à geração de renda para famílias em situação de vulnerabilidade social.

Criado em 2021 pelo (DAEP), o Projeto Sol, Programa de Saneamento Solidário, oferece oportunidades de trabalho para moradores. O trabalho é organizado em jornadas flexíveis, de acordo com a disponibilidade de cada pessoa e as demandas do município. Os participantes recebem um auxílio mensal de R$ 722.

A flexibilidade permite que mulheres conciliem a atividade com outros compromissos profissionais e familiares. É o caso de Edilene Santos, que trabalha como enfermeira e aproveita os dias de folga para participar do projeto.

Projeto Sol, Programa de Saneamento Solidário, oferece oportunidades de trabalho para moradores em Penápolis — Foto: TV TEM/ Reprodução

"Eu trabalho na Santa Casa numa escala 12x36, então, dia sim e outro não, estou livre. Então, peguei esse compromisso para ajudar na minha renda. Tem sido muito bom", relata.

A maioria das vagas é ocupada por mulheres, muitas delas mães que precisam conciliar os cuidados com a família e outras atividades profissionais com a busca por uma renda complementar.

Além do benefício financeiro, o projeto contribui para a conservação da cidade e incentiva a participação da população no cuidado com os espaços coletivos.

O cadastro para participar do Projeto Sol é gratuito. As oportunidades são disponibilizadas ao longo do ano, conforme a demanda do município e a disponibilidade de vagas. É preciso acompanhar os períodos de chamamento público e realizar a inscrição presencialmente.

articles.title: Vítima é socorrida em estado grave após acidente em Jundiaí | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo informações da concessionária, um dos veículos fugiu após a batida no sábado (14). Outras duas pessoas tiveram ferimentos leves.
articles.summary: Uma vítima foi socorrida em estado grave após se envolver em um acidente entre dois carros na Rodovia dos Bandeirantes (SP-348), em Jundiaí (SP), na manhã deste sábado (14).
articles.body:
Vítima foi socorrida em estado grave — Foto: Artesp/Divulgação

Um acidente entre dois carros na Rodovia dos Bandeirantes (SP-348), em Jundiaí (SP), na manhã de sábado (14), deixou um ferido em estado grave.

Segundo a concessionária que administra a via, o acidente aconteceu no quilômetro 66, da pista sentido interior. Os dois carros bateram, com um deles capotando em seguida.

Um dos veículos envolvidos no ocorrido fugiu e não havia sido encontrado até a publicação desta reportagem. Outras duas pessoas tiveram ferimentos leves.

Ainda conforme a concessionária, o acostamento e a faixa 3 precisaram ser interditados devido ao acidente. Os envolvidos foram socorridos pelo Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu) e levados para uma unidade hospitalar.

Apesar das fotos mostrarem lentidão, a concessionária informou que não havia registro de congestionamento no trecho.

articles.title: VÍDEO: Menina indígena do Acre cobra demarcação de terras na COP31 | G1
articles.standfirst: Na conferência, que ocorre na Turquia, Luna Manchineri, de 10 anos, pede que as crianças indígenas sejam ouvidas nas decisões sobre o futuro da floresta.
articles.summary: Na conferência, que ocorre na Turquia, Luna Manchineri, de 10 anos, pede que as crianças indígenas sejam ouvidas nas decisões sobre o futuro da floresta.
articles.body:
Com apenas 10 anos, a pequena Luna Manchineri cobrou o avanço da demarcação das terras indígenas e a participação das crianças nas decisões sobre o futuro da Amazônia durante a 31ª Conferência das Nações Unidas sobre Mudanças Climáticas (COP31), que ocorre em Antália, na Turquia. (Veja vídeo acima)

Luna representou as crianças indígenas da Amazônia Brasileira e defendeu que a proteção da floresta precisa considerar os territórios indígenas e garantir que as próximas gerações possam continuar vivendo neles.

Durante sua participação, na última quarta-feira (11), a jovem também entregou uma carta escrita à mão à primeira-dama Janja Lula da Silva, com o pedido de que a mensagem fosse encaminhada ao presidente Lula.

Segundo a mãe da menina, a gestora de formação e diretora-executiva da organização indígena Manxinerune Tsihi Pukte Hajene (Matpha), Wauana Manchineri, de 32 anos, a expectativa é que o documento ajude a abrir espaço para que as reivindicações das crianças sejam ouvidas pelo governo federal. Ela acompanhou a filha na conferência como representante da organização.

Luna Manchineri tem 10 anos e cobrou a demarcação das terras indígenas durante a COP31 — Foto: Reprodução

Ao g1 , ela contou que Luna acompanha o movimento indígena desde antes de nascer e que demonstra interesse pelas questões ambientais. A previsão é que a delegação retorne na próxima segunda-feira (16) para acompanhar as agendas dos presidentes.

Ainda de acordo com Wauana, a primeira-dama disse que tentaria viabilizar a conversa, mas a agenda não permitiu que o encontro ocorresse durante a conferência.

“Estamos esperando com esperança que esse momento possa acontecer e pedimos apoio à Marina Silva, Marco Tulio, alguns outros parceiros e à Janja também”, explicou.

Wauana Manchineri participa da COP31 com a filha — Foto: Vicente Taveira/Ascom Coiab

Em um vídeo, Luna apresenta uma manifestação na COP31. Em seu posicionamento, a menina destacou a importância da liderança brasileira no combate ao desmatamento. Além disso, ela lembrou ainda que a conservação da Amazônia está diretamente ligada à proteção dos territórios indígenas.

“Agora desejamos que a demarcação das terras indígenas avance cada vez mais. Pergunto para todos aqui: ‘Quem irá defender a Amazônia e o Brasil em 2050?’ ”, questionou.

A jovem também chamou a atenção para a perspectiva de quem ainda vai estar vivendo as consequências das decisões tomadas neste e nos próximos anos. Ao comparar sua idade atual com a que terá em 2050, Luna destacou que o futuro da floresta diz respeito às crianças que vivem nos territórios indígenas.

“Hoje eu tenho 10 anos, em 2050 terei 34. Por isso estou aqui. Em 2050, quero estar ao lado dos meus amigos, vivendo na nossa floresta. Nós crianças indígenas também temos voz e corremos o risco de não ter um território vivo para o nosso futuro. A resposta somos nós ”, declarou.

Segundo Wauana, a menina participa do CAFI Parentinho, uma iniciativa da Coordenação das Organizações Indígenas da Amazônia Brasileira (Coiab) voltada às crianças indígenas da Amazônia.

De acordo com ela, o espaço promove a construção política com a participação infantil e busca ampliar a presença das crianças nos debates sobre os direitos dos povos indígenas e a proteção dos territórios.

A carta que fundamenta a mobilização e entregue a Janja, segundo Wauana, foi construída coletivamente durante o Acampamento Terra Livre (ATL). “A carta é construída com as crianças durante o Acampamento Terra Livre. Já temos o ‘Manifesto das Crianças Indígenas da Amazônia Brasileira’ e a carta de incidência da COP”, disse.

Wauana também mencionou o chamado ‘Mapa do Caminho’, descrito na carta, e que defende que iniciativas como esta sejam acompanhadas pelo avanço da demarcação e por mecanismos que permitam a participação efetiva das crianças indígenas.

“Na carta do primeiro momento ela fala sobre o protagonismo do Brasil como líder de preservação, mas lembra que a preservação vem principalmente dos territórios indígenas, fala que o Mapa do Caminho é uma boa solução do Brasil para os demais países, mas que esse mecanismo traga a demarcação do território e, principalmente, pede que as vozes das crianças indígenas realmente sejam ouvidas, que tenha um espaço que elas possam estar e construir políticas e mecanismo ao olhar e jeitos delas”, afirmou.

articles.title: Médico pode ser punido por usar energia de UBS para carregar carro | G1
articles.standfirst: Especialista em Direito Público afirma que utilização de recurso público para benefício privado é irregular quando não há autorização ou justificativa. Caso foi registrado em Pará de Minas.
articles.summary: Especialista afirma que utilização de recurso público para benefício privado é irregular quando não há autorização ou justificativa. Caso foi registrado em Pará de Minas.
articles.body:
A utilização da energia elétrica de uma Unidade Básica de Saúde (UBS) para carregar o carro particular de um médico pode configurar uso irregular de recurso público e resultar em responsabilização administrativa do servidor .

A avaliação é do advogado especialista em Direito Público João Gontijo, ouvido pelo g1 após a repercussão de um vídeo que mostra o profissional usando uma tomada da unidade para recarregar o veículo particular, em Pará de Minas , no Centro-Oeste de Minas.

Segundo o especialista, a Administração Pública deve seguir o princípio da finalidade pública, que determina que bens e recursos sejam utilizados em benefício da coletividade e não para atender a interesses particulares.

"Assim, a utilização de energia elétrica de um órgão para recarregar veículo particular de servidor, sem autorização ou justificativa vinculada ao serviço público, é uma conduta irregular, pois representa o emprego de recurso público em benefício privado, podendo ensejar a apuração de eventual responsabilidade administrativa do servidor", explicou.

João ressalta, no entanto, que a análise da legalidade depende da finalidade da utilização do recurso.

"A ilegalidade da conduta está sempre vinculada à finalidade da utilização, se para atender ao interesse público ou privado", afirmou.

O caso veio à tona após um vídeo circular nas redes sociais mostrando um médico recarregando o próprio carro elétrico em uma UBS de Pará de Minas. Nas imagens, o veículo aparece estacionado sobre a calçada, enquanto uma extensão atravessa o muro até uma tomada na área externa da unidade.

Segundo a Prefeitura, o carro pertence a um médico vinculado ao governo federal como bolsista do Programa Mais Médicos para o Brasil.

Prefeitura vai pedir procedimento disciplinar

Em nota, a prefeitura classificou o episódio como uma grave intercorrência e afirmou que repudia qualquer tipo de desvio de finalidade do patrimônio público. O profissional será notificado pela Secretaria Municipal de Saúde, junto à Procuradoria-Geral do Município.

A ocorrência também será comunicada à Comissão de Coordenação Estadual (CCE) e à Coordenação Nacional do programa, vinculada à Secretaria de Gestão do Trabalho e da Educação na Saúde (SGTES), do Ministério da Saúde.

O objetivo é formalizar a comunicação dos fatos e solicitar a instauração de um procedimento disciplinar para avaliar a aplicação das penalidades previstas nas normas do programa.

articles.title: In 1944, a US paratrooper left his fiancée’s letters in Belgium; 66 years later, the box returned to the couple, who had married in 1946
articles.summary: Discover the incredible story of how a box of treasured letters from WWII returned to a paratrooper and his wife after decades, reminding us of the enduring power of love and memories.
articles.body: Imagine losing a box of your most treasured messages, then getting it back on a random day decades later. That's what happened to John Alfred D’Amore and his wife, Rose, according to a United Service Organisations (USO) story. John was 21 in 1944, a private first class in Headquarters Company, 82nd Airborne Division. There were no barracks, so he lived with a local family in Nandrin, Belgium, where he kept a hand-carved wooden box filled with letters from his fiancée, Rose Archie, as well as photos of friends and fellow soldiers. He hoped to carry it back home one day. Instead, he ended up in hospital with a broken ankle and never went back to the house, so the box remained where he had left it. John returned home safe and sound. On 29 June 1946, he and Rose got married in Niagara Falls, New York. They later had two children, two grandchildren, and two great-grandchildren.Why letters mattered, and a surprise in the attic Letters were a lifeline for soldiers in those times. In a Library of Congress article about wartime correspondence, it is explained that letters and telegrams were virtually the only way to communicate between service members and civilians. The letters provided comfort for those enduring loneliness and fighting in war. News from home, or the lack thereof, could have had a major impact on morale. Hence, Rose’s letters meant much more than just a piece of paper; they were her voice, close at hand in terrifying times. Then in early June 2011, Anne-Marie Radelet, a Belgian lady, was cleaning up the attic of her late father-in-law when she discovered the box. It had a name and a place of origin on its cover. Realising that somebody had lost their memories, she gave it to the Ardennes American Cemetery employee. The American Battle Monuments Commission places the cemetery near Neupré, 12 miles southwest of Liège.A race to bring it home The cemetery's superintendent, Alan Amelinckx, read some of the letters for clues, then searched online for the name on the box, but found nothing. He then called the city clerk in Niagara Falls, and after a few more phone calls, he got John's son, John David D’Amore. The real surprise came next: John and Rose were alive and living in Florida near their son. But there was one problem. Amelinckx was not able to cover the postage with government funds. He thought the box should be returned to the family. He recalled a family he had taken on a tour around the cemetery the summer before. Their father, Gerald Leary, was the regional president for Europe, the Middle East, the Indian subcontinent, and Africa for FedEx. Leary had offered help if ever needed. Amelinckx called him, and a FedEx courier picked up the box that same day.The kitchen table moment The day of delivery saw the family waiting at John David's house for the FedEx van. The two veterans stepped out of the van and carried the box inside. About 15 people sat down in the kitchen while John David unpacked the box and laid out the contents: letters, several 82nd Airborne patches and ribbons and wartime photographs. John looked at the pictures he had taken and, while his short-term memory was impaired, he remembered names, places and situations, from driving entertainers Marlene Dietrich and Bob Hope to landing behind enemy lines in a glider. Rose recognised the card, and pictures she had sent him and her first comment, as her son recalled, was that she hoped she hadn't said anything bad. Only a few weeks later, the couple celebrated their 65th wedding anniversary. John David plans to keep the box in the family so the history will not be forgotten. The story can be a gentle reminder that some keepsakes are worth saving, and perhaps worth passing on to someone who will be glad of them one day.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: At 80, Helen Thayer undertook another demanding trek: after becoming the first woman to trek solo to the Magnetic North Pole at 50, she walked the full length of Death Valley alone in 2017
articles.summary: Helen Thayer, at 80 years old, made history by becoming the first person to walk the full length of Death Valley, following a remarkable life of exploration that includes becoming the first woman to trek solo to the Magnetic North Pole.
articles.body: Helen Thayer was 50 when she became the first woman to make a solo, unresupplied ski trek to the Magnetic North Pole. Nearly three decades later, she took on another demanding journey. In November 2017, at the age of 80 years, Thayer started walking all the way from one end of Death Valley, California, pulling her supplies in a cart, according to WINGS WorldQuest’s interview with her. This 212-mile walk was another record for the explorer. Before this, Thayer had experienced some of the toughest terrains around the globe. Thayer has also travelled across Arctic ice, crossed major deserts and paddled down the Amazon River. At 80, she was still taking on demanding challenges.A solo journey to the Magnetic North Pole at 50Thayer’s Arctic expedition occurred in 1988. Thayer embarked on this Arctic adventure at the age of 50 and alone, with only her dog, Charlie, to accompany her on this trek to the Magnetic North Pole. She went on the journey without any outside help and became the first woman known to make the trip. Thayer completed the Arctic expedition without receiving food or supplies from outside parties, accompanied by her dog. She later spoke about the experience at Fort Jackson, South Carolina, where she discussed exploration and the challenges of travelling through the Arctic. The trip was also incorporated into her educational work. In 1988, she started the Adventure Classroom program in which she used her adventures to teach children about geography and nature.Walking 212 miles through Death Valley at 80Thayer embarked on yet another solo trek in November 2017 at the age of 80. The trek involved hiking the full length of Death Valley from its northern end. The journey comprised 212 miles. Unlike previous ventures, Thayer did not carry all the gear on her back. Instead, she pulled her stuff using a cart, Molly, weighing 185 pounds at the start of the expedition.Thayer made it through. Later, in an interview with WINGS WorldQuest, she stated that she had been informed she was the first person to make a trek of the absolute full length of Death Valley. She was informed of this distinction since she had taken the route from the northernmost point of the valley and not from the shorter path. A year later, she made the same trek together with her shepherd-golden retriever, Sam. The details of both journeys appeared in WINGS WorldQuest’s interview with Thayer, published in 2019.A lifetime spent exploring the worldThe Death Valley trip of Thayer was part of a much broader mission to explore America’s national parks. Thayer’s project included creating technical reports, photographs, videos, children’s books and educational material for students. Moreover, she also had the goal of motivating the young generation to get out and appreciate the natural wealth of America. With the help of her Adventure Classroom program, she used actual expeditions to motivate students to learn about nature.Her accomplishments were not limited to the Arctic and Death Valley. According to WINGS WorldQuest, Thayer was the first woman to walk across the Sahara and Gobi deserts. Her Gobi expedition covered 1,600 miles across Mongolia in 2001, a journey she completed with her husband, Bill. From her solo ski trek to the Magnetic North Pole at 50 to her 212-mile walk through the Death Valley at 80, Thayer continued exploring long after many people would have stepped away from such demanding challenges. Her story also showed how she used those experiences to encourage younger generations to discover and protect the natural world.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.body: CHANDIGARH: Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann on Saturday launched a quiz competition, 'Punjab Da Crorepati', for youngsters in the state, with the winner set to receive a cash prize of Rs 1 crore.Announcing the initiative, Mann said the competition would test participants' knowledge of Punjab's history, culture, geography, mathematics and various aspects of the state government.Youngsters aged between 15 and 30 years will be eligible to participate, he said."The Punjab government is launching a unique programme for youths -- ‘Punjab Da Crorepati’," Mann said during the launch.The competition will comprise 11 rounds, with nine to be conducted through an online portal and the remaining two held in person, according to details shared by the chief minister."There will be questions like (the TV quiz show) 'Kaun Banega Crorepati', and there will be four options," he said.The quiz will have a pool of 50,000 questions, most of which will be based on questions asked in recruitment examinations for government jobs, including those for patwaris, constables, Punjab Civil Services officers and sub-divisional officers, Mann said.The tenth round will be held across 23 districts, with the toppers from each district qualifying for the grand finale.A total of 10,000 participants will receive prizes, he said.At the grand finale, the winner will receive Rs 1 crore, while four runners-up will each get Rs 10 lakh, according to the chief minister.Mann urged schools and colleges across the state to register for the competition.(With Agency Inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chandigarh | Silver Rate in Chandigarh | Bank Holidays in Chandigarh | Public Holidays in Chandigarh | Chandigarh AQI | Weather in Chandigarh | Petrol Price in Chandigarh | Diesel Price in Chandigarh | CNG Price in Chandigarh | LPG Price in ChandigarhStay updated with the latest Chandigarh news. articles.title: Ukraine's Nato bid back on table, but at what cost? Zelenskyy reveals US question on Donbas
articles.summary: Ukraine's long-standing ambition to join Nato has resurfaced in peace negotiations with Russia, but a potentially difficult question now hangs over Kyiv's
articles.body: Ukraine's long-standing ambition to join Nato has resurfaced in peace negotiations with Russia, but a potentially difficult question now hangs over Kyiv's bid.Would Ukraine be willing to give up the Donbas in return for membership of the military alliance? US negotiators have raised the question, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said, signalling that territorial concessions and security guarantees could become central to efforts to end the war.In a series of statements to reporters, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said he believed Nato membership was "back on the agenda", revealing that US negotiators had asked whether Ukraine was prepared to surrender the Donbas in exchange for joining the alliance, Reuters reported.Zelenskyy's remarks come amid renewed diplomatic efforts to end the war, with Washington seeking to bring Moscow and Kyiv closer to a possible settlement.He said US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner had told him that Russian President Vladimir Putin had agreed to have European representatives participate in the next round of peace talks.The Ukrainian president said he had asked European allies to decide by the end of November who would represent the continent at the negotiating table. Kyiv wants Europe to have a direct say in any agreement that could determine Ukraine's territorial future and long-term security arrangements.However, prospects for even a limited ceasefire remain uncertain. Zelenskyy said Russia was unwilling to agree to an energy ceasefire and that its delegation did not have the mandate to discuss the proposal during talks in Abu Dhabi.Zelenskyy also flagged continued restrictions on the US-operated Starshield satellite system, saying its high-speed capabilities had still not been restored despite being needed for Ukrainian military operations along the front line and in Russian-occupied areas.Meanwhile, Zelenskyy is seeking to strengthen Ukraine's military capabilities through fresh European assistance, with Kyiv discussing the supply of 800,000 rounds of ammunition for its F-16 fighter jets with Denmark to meet the aircraft's requirements for six months, Reuters reported.The discussions come as Ukraine seeks to sustain its fleet of Western-supplied fighter jets amid continued Russian aerial attacks. The F-16s play an important role in protecting Ukrainian airspace, intercepting Russian drones and cruise missiles, and countering aerial threats. Securing a steady supply of ammunition is therefore crucial to maintaining their operational effectiveness.In a post on X following his visits to Denmark and Ireland, Zelenskyy announced a new €645 million defence package and a separate €20 million energy assistance package from Denmark. The defence package includes support for F-16 ammunition, attack drones, Ukrainian interceptor drones and contributions to the Prioritised Ukraine Requirements List (PURL) programme.Zelenskyy said Ukraine had also discussed with its European partners ways to strengthen air defence and support its energy sector and railway network ahead of winter. The discussions focused on securing assistance to protect critical infrastructure and help the country withstand further Russian attacks.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Germany produces 6 million tonnes of waste-incineration ash annually; scientists are testing whether the hazardous residue can absorb CO2 and become a material for road construction and concrete
articles.summary: Germany produces around 6 million tonnes of ash from municipal waste incineration every year, leaving behind a substantial residue that requires careful
articles.body: Germany produces around 6 million tonnes of ash from municipal waste incineration every year, leaving behind a substantial residue that requires careful treatment. Researchers are now investigating whether this material can serve a useful purpose beyond waste management. A project involving TH Köln(Cologne University of Applied Sciences) and RWTH Aachen University is testing methods to make the ash absorb and permanently retain carbon dioxide, potentially transforming it into a resource for road construction and concrete production. The approach could also reduce the need for construction materials extracted through energy-intensive processes.How Germany is turning waste ash into a carbon-storing construction materialThe research centres on bottom ash, the mineral-rich residue left after municipal waste is burned. Although it contains materials that could be useful in construction, untreated incineration ash is considered hazardous because it can contain heavy metals, toxic dioxins, furans and soluble salts, according to Engineers Ireland.The residue is therefore not directly suitable for use in building projects. Before it can become a potential construction resource, it must undergo processing to recover metals and remove unwanted contaminants.TH Köln explains that specialised facilities already handle this material through metal recovery, screening and sorting. These steps produce a cleaned ash that can be examined for further applications.The researchers are now exploring whether the mineral components in this processed residue can also help address CO2 emissions. The idea is to use the ash's natural ability to react with carbon dioxide, creating a material that stores the gas while potentially serving another industrial purpose.Carbonation offers a way to bind carbon dioxide permanentlyThe central process being investigated is carbonation, a chemical reaction in which minerals within the ash absorb carbon dioxide and bind it into a more stable form.According to TH Köln, the mineral content of the processed ash can take up carbon dioxide and retain it permanently. Researchers want to develop a practical method for making this reaction work efficiently outside laboratory conditions.The project is led by the Bergischer Abfallwirtschaftsverband, or BAV, with TH Köln and RWTH Aachen University participating as scientific partners. The industrial partner refer GmbH is supplying processed incineration ash from its treatment facility.The work is part of KARMA, a project focused on carbonation of waste-incineration ash. The initiative secured funding through North Rhine-Westphalia's CCU model regions competition and will receive more than one million euros in support until mid-2028. CCU refers to capturing carbon dioxide and putting it to use rather than simply releasing it into the atmosphere.Which carbonation method can capture more carbonA major part of the research involves comparing two different ways of bringing carbon dioxide into contact with the ash. The methods differ in how much moisture they use and how effectively the gas can penetrate the material.The first method is wet carbonation, where the ash is processed in water. This method allows for more CO2 absorption, but it needs energy. Then the material has to be dried, which may affect the overall efficiency of the process.The second way is to use limited moisture. In this method a carbonated layer is formed on the surface of the ash. But the layer can get quite dense and keep carbon dioxide from getting deeper into the material. This means less gas is being stored.”These trade-offs were outlined by Axel Wellendorf of TH Köln, who explained that both approaches have advantages and disadvantages. The researchers need to determine which method offers the most suitable balance between carbon uptake and the energy required to process the material.A test facility will compare the different approachesTo move the research beyond lab experiments, the partners are developing a technical test facility at the Leppe waste disposal centre near Lindlar in Germany.The facility is being established by TH Köln and RWTH Aachen University and will be operated by BAV, which leads the project. The processed ash supplied by refer GmbH will provide the starting material for experiments.The planned facility will allow the researchers to adjust and compare different carbonation methods under conditions closer to practical industrial use.Engineers Ireland reports that the project is intended to develop a flexible pilot system capable of testing the processes under realistic conditions. The researchers will first evaluate how the ash reacts with carbon dioxide before examining whether the resulting material can meet construction requirements.Could carbonated ash replace sand and gravel in roadsOne of the possible applications is road construction, where carbonated ash could be used in an unbound form. This means the material would not necessarily need to be incorporated into concrete or another binding mixture before being used.TH Köln says the processed ash could potentially replace gravel or sand in road construction and earthworks. These materials are commonly obtained through extraction, which can require considerable energy.By using carbonated ash instead, the project hopes to substitute some of these conventional raw materials with a residue that would otherwise require further management.The researchers are also examining whether the material could be suitable for concrete production. In this application, the ash could potentially function as a binder rather than simply replacing aggregates such as sand or gravel.But concrete production places stricter demands on the consistency of the materials used. The ash must have a defined and reliable quality to ensure that it can perform as intended. TH Köln says achieving the required standards would represent an important contribution to the circular economy and climate protection.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: US flight chaos: Trump official seeks $50 billion for air traffic control overhaul after nationwide disruptions
articles.summary: The Trump administration has raised its demand for air traffic control funding to $50 billion after a communications failure triggered a nationwide ground
articles.body: The Trump administration has raised its demand for air traffic control funding to $50 billion after a communications failure triggered a nationwide ground stop in the United States on Friday, disrupting thousands of flights for several hours.Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the incident exposed the urgent need to replace the country's ageing air traffic control infrastructure, calling on Congress to approve billions of dollars for a complete overhaul of the system."This is an emergency. What's more important than having an air traffic control system that actually works?" Duffy said on Friday.The administration had initially sought $30.1 billion for upgrading the country's airports and air traffic control network. However, following the disruption, Duffy said he wanted $50 billion to complete the modernisation effort."What we have is an incredibly old air traffic control system," he said, adding that the government needed new hardware, software and telecommunications infrastructure rather than temporary fixes.What caused the nationwide flight disruption?The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ordered a nationwide ground stop at around 4 pm EST on Friday after a communications problem affected its en route centres, which manage aircraft movement between airports.Duffy said an overload of data on routers and switches led to inconsistencies in information being transmitted through the system, forcing officials to halt operations.The ground stop remained in place for nearly four hours before the FAA lifted it at around 8:15 pm. However, Duffy warned that it would take time for flight operations to return to normal.Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said officials had found no evidence of a cyberattack behind the disruption, although investigations were continuing. He also said the public was never in danger during the incident.Why is the US seeking billions for air traffic control?The FAA continues to rely on ageing technology, including decades-old computers and replacement parts purchased through online auction websites. Last week, the agency said it planned to phase out floppy disks used to transmit weather and other critical information at more than 400 air traffic control facilities by the end of 2028.The administration's initial $30.1 billion funding request included $10.1 billion for air traffic control modernisation, including $7.2 billion for a common automation platform and controller workstations, and $2 billion for cloud computing.It also sought $2 billion to replace and upgrade FAA control towers and $18 billion for airport-related projects, including $10 billion to modernise or replace ageing terminals.The administration has said the investment would help build a more reliable telecommunications network, upgrade equipment and improve airport infrastructure.Congress had already approved $12.5 billion over five years in July 2025 to modernise air traffic control systems and increase the recruitment of controllers.The latest disruption comes amid a series of incidents involving the country's aviation infrastructure. In September, a circuit failure at a Philadelphia air traffic facility and an accidentally severed fibre-optic cable in New Jersey caused thousands of flight delays and cancellations across the northeastern US.The country has also faced concerns over aviation safety following a midair collision near Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport in January 2025 that killed 67 people.The administration is urging the Republican-led Congress to approve the additional funding before the end of the year. Democrats are scheduled to take control of Congress in January.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Nikki Haley’s son backs her decision to skip 2028 race after Republican midterm losses
articles.summary: Nalin Haley, son of former US ambassador to the United Nations and former South Carolina governor Nikki Haley, has defended his mother's decision to stay
articles.body: Nalin Haley, son of former US ambassador to the United Nations and former South Carolina governor Nikki Haley, has defended his mother's decision to stay out of the 2028 presidential race, hitting back at critics questioning her political future. Responding to a social media user who mocked her decision, Nalin said his mother had made the right call and accused her critics of holding personal grudges against her.Nalin's remarks come after he questioned the Republican Party's performance in the midterm elections, arguing that it had failed to make use of its control over the White House, House of Representatives and Senate."We primarily lost not cuz of what we did, but what we didn't do. We had control of the house, senate, and presidency. What did we do with it? Nothing!" he wrote in a post on X.Nalin hits back at critic over Nikki Haley's 2028 decisionNalin came to his mother's defence after social media user Justin Evans mocked her decision not to pursue another presidential campaign in 2028."There are like 14 people at a private club in Southampton, NY, absolutely devastated by this news," Evans wrote in a post reacting to Haley's announcement.Responding to him, Nalin questioned Evans' political track record and brought up a gubernatorial campaign that ended in a significant defeat despite considerable financial resources and political backing."Justin one day when you grow old, you'll realize holding a grudge because Nikki Haley fired you 17 years ago is not healthy. It's pathetic actually. Maybe if you focused less on her, you wouldn't be responsible for the worst ran gubernatorial race of all time," Nalin wrote.His response suggested that the continued criticism of his mother was rooted in a long-standing personal dispute.Nikki Haley rules out 2028 presidential bidNikki Haley has made it clear that she does not intend to seek the Republican presidential nomination in 2028, although she plans to remain involved in politics.Speaking on Bloomberg Television's *Balance of Power*, Haley said she would continue advocating for policies she supports and backing candidates."I am not running in 2028, but I will continue to talk about the things that I care about. I will continue to push good policy. I will continue to support good candidates, and we want a strong America. And whatever we have to do, I think every one of us has an obligation to try," she said.Haley also argued that Republicans should focus on addressing voters' concerns before turning their attention to choosing the party's next presidential nominee.She pointed to inflation, the rising cost of living and high interest rates as pressing economic challenges that the party had not adequately addressed.Rubio, Vance among potential Republican contenders for 2028With Haley ruling herself out, speculation has intensified over who could emerge as the Republican Party's presidential candidate in 2028.Vice-President JD Vance, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Texas Senator Ted Cruz are among the potential contenders being discussed. Donald Trump Jr., the US president's eldest son, has also been mentioned as a possible political successor to his father.A Reuters/Ipsos poll indicated that Rubio had a slight advantage among Republican voters, with 45% describing him as an excellent potential presidential candidate. Vance followed at 43%, while Florida Governor Ron DeSantis received 32%.Haley challenged Donald Trump for the Republican presidential nomination during the 2024 election cycle before suspending her campaign.Although she has now ruled out another presidential bid, her latest remarks indicate that she intends to remain active in shaping Republican politics through policy advocacy and support for candidates.You use AI every day. articles.title: Apparel industry sees sign of export revival
articles.summary: TIRUPUR: India’s ready-made garment (RMG) exports rose 20% in October 2026 compared to October 2025, while growth in rupee terms stood at 30%, Apparel
articles.body: TIRUPUR: India’s ready-made garment (RMG) exports rose 20% in October 2026 compared to October 2025, while growth in rupee terms stood at 30%, Apparel Export Promotion Council (AEPC) chairman Dr A Sakthivel has said, calling the performance a sign of revival in the apparel export industry.“The 20% growth in RMG exports in October 2026 is a very encouraging development. The industry has abundant orders in hand, and the immediate priority is to ensure adequate workforce availability to meet the growing demand,” he said in a statement on Saturday.According to Dr Sakthivel, exporters are seeing an improving business environment and are holding a strong pipeline of orders from overseas buyers, indicating firmer demand for Indian garments across key international markets. “The near-term constraint for the sector is the availability of adequate workforce to execute orders on time and at scale,” he said.Labour availability has emerged as the immediate operational challenge even as order books strengthen. Addressing the gap will require focused skilling initiatives, labour mobilisation and supportive measures so that exporters can convert existing orders into higher shipments and sustain momentum in coming months, according to him.AEPC is facilitating market outreach opportunities for member exporters to explore and expand presence in major destinations. The council’s planned initiatives include engagements in Japan, London, Denmark, New York, Las Vegas, France and Dubai, along with participation in Bharat Tex ’27, positioned as a global platform bringing together the Indian textile and apparel value chain.He urged exporters to use AEPC-supported platforms to build new business connections, tap emerging markets, diversify export destinations and secure additional orders, as competition intensifies and buyers seek supply resilience.Dr Sakthivel linked the sector’s growth prospects to improved market access through free trade agreements and faster resolution of workforce-related constraints. articles.title: In 1997, Ted Turner heard how a Mississippi washerwoman gave $150,000 of her savings for scholarships and pledged $1 billion to support UN causes; his daughter now says another $3 billion followed
articles.summary: Ted Turner’s decision to give $1 billion to the United Nations in 1997 was inspired by a story he heard about a washerwoman in Mississippi who donated her
articles.body: Ted Turner’s decision to give $1 billion to the United Nations in 1997 was inspired by a story he heard about a washerwoman in Mississippi who donated her life savings of $150,000 for college scholarships. His daughter, Laura Turner Seydel, shared that detail at a celebration of his life at the United Nations, where she also revealed that another $3 billion had since been donated to match his original gift, reported the Associated Press (AP).Turner, who founded CNN and became one of the most influential figures in global media, died in May at the age of 87 after a long battle with Lewy body dementia. His legacy, according to those who knew him, extends far beyond broadcasting and into the world of philanthropy, environmentalism and international cooperation. Read more, as per AP, here:The story that inspired a billion-dollar giftTurner’s daughter recounted how her father was moved by the story of the washerwoman, whose act of generosity struck a deep chord with him. He reportedly said that if she could give so much from so little, then he would have to do something equally significant.That moment led directly to his announcement at a UN gala dinner in September 1997, where he pledged $1 billion to support UN causes. At the time, it was the largest individual donation in history.The gift was used to establish the United Nations Foundation, an organisation created to channel private donations to UN programmes. articles.title: Grandmother mistakes medieval gold cross for costume jewelry before learning its five-figure value
articles.summary: A United Kingdom grandmother nearly tossed the medieval gold reliquary cross aside as costume jewelry before fellow hobbyists confirmed it was real gold.
articles.body: A grandmother recently discovered a medieval gold cross while metal detecting in a farmer's field — and it could be worth tens of thousands of dollars. The cross was found by 58-year-old metal detecting hobbyist Shelley Couzins in August, news agency Southwest News Service (SWNS) reported. The discovery was only recently publicized. Couzins, a grandmother of five who took up metal detecting four years ago, told SWNS she was out with a group on the Isle of Sheppey in Kent in the United Kingdom when, after five hours of searching, she found nothing but "rubbish." MYSTERIOUS FIND BENEATH FIELD LEADS MAN TO MASSIVE TREASURE HIDDEN FOR CENTURIES Around lunchtime, her metal detector suddenly began beeping, prompting her to dig roughly 12 inches into the freshly plowed soil. "It was quite quiet all morning, and then I heard this beep," Couzins recalled. She soon unearthed a gold cross — but initially dismissed it as costume jewelry. It wasn't until she returned to the group's main tent that fellow hobbyists told her the cross was made of real gold. REAL-LIFE EXCALIBUR? MAN ON A HIKE UNCOVERS GOLD SWORD RELIC HIDDEN UNDER TREE "It is like a metal detectorist's dream," Couzins told SWNS. "You only find something like this once in a lifetime." Couzins was searching with a group called Medway History Finders, which has withheld the field's exact location over concerns about illegal treasure hunters. The cross, which weighs 10.6 grams, was subsequently reported to a Finds Liaison Officer under England's treasure reporting process. MYSTERY DEEPENS AFTER 2,700-YEAR-OLD BRONZE SWORD EMERGES STANDING UPRIGHT The grandmother said she was "absolutely gutted" about having to surrender the artifact. "I like to keep everything I find. I know I will probably never see it again," Couzins said. "I am happy for it to go to a good home, where it needs to go, instead of sitting in my cupboard." The artifact was identified as a medieval gold reliquary cross, depicting Jesus' crucifixion on one side and the Virgin Mary holding baby Jesus on the other, according to SWNS. The cross can also be opened to hold religious relics, though Couzins said she left it sealed for fear of damaging it. 2,000-YEAR-OLD TREASURE DISCOVERED BENEATH FORMER SPORTS FIELD, BREAKING REGIONAL RECORD The artifact is being assessed by the British Museum, according to SWNS. Its ultimate ownership and value have yet to be determined. If acquired through the treasure process, the cross would be valued, with any resulting reward expected to be split between Couzins and the landowner. Online estimates have placed the cross's potential value at a minimum of £20,000 (roughly $27,000), though no official valuation has been announced, said SWNS. Couzins also expressed relief that the delicate artifact had survived the plowing of the field without being destroyed. articles.title: Bangladesh garment owners threaten to quit wage talks, shut factories indefinitely
articles.summary: Garment manufacturers in Bangladesh have threatened to withdraw from minimum wage negotiations and shut factories indefinitely if workers continue
articles.body: Garment manufacturers in Bangladesh have threatened to withdraw from minimum wage negotiations and shut factories indefinitely if workers continue vandalising industrial units during protests.The Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) and Bangladesh Knitwear Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BKMEA) said on Saturday that they were reconsidering their participation in the wage talks, citing a lack of assurances over factory security."If the situation persists, we must reconsider," BGMEA president Mahmud Hasan Khan said at a news briefing in Dhaka, referring to the next round of negotiations scheduled for Monday.Khan also said factories unable to operate because of the unrest would remain closed indefinitely under Bangladesh's labour law. Section 13(1) of the Bangladesh Labour Act allows employers to suspend operations under a "no work, no pay" provision.The warning comes after weeks of protests over wages and working conditions, with demonstrations turning violent in several garment manufacturing centres. Workers have blocked roads, while clashes this month have involved damage to property and the torching of police vehicles.At least 147 factories remained closed on Saturday across Savar, Ashulia and Gazipur, the country's major garment manufacturing hubs. More than 4,500 factories are registered with industry trade bodies.Wage talks face fresh uncertaintyThe Minimum Wage Board, formed on November 1, is due to meet on Monday to discuss a revised pay structure for garment workers. The current minimum monthly wage stands at Tk12,500 (approx INR 9479), fixed in December 2023.Workers' representatives have proposed raising the minimum to Tk32,000 (approx INR 24267), more than double the existing rate, according to local media reports. The demand has also been reported at Tk30,000 (approx INR 22751) in other accounts.The workers' proposal includes Tk19,200 (approx INR 14560) in basic pay, Tk9,600 (approx INR 7280) in house rent and Tk3,200 (approx INR 2426) in allowances covering medical expenses, transport, food and other costs. It also proposes four wage grades, with monthly salaries ranging from Tk32,000 (approx INR 24267) to Tk48,000 (approx INR 36401).Factory owners have yet to submit their formal proposal. They were given four days after the November 9 meeting to prepare their recommendations, which are expected to be discussed at Monday's session. Local media reports said employers could submit their proposal while staying away from the meeting.Workers say their wages have failed to keep pace with the rising cost of food, housing, transport and healthcare. Inflation in Bangladesh is running at around 8%, further eroding their purchasing power.The minimum wage has risen consistently in Bangladesh but despite these increases, Bangladesh's garment workers remain among the lower-paid in the region.The threat of an indefinite shutdown has already materialised at several units. Seven factories in Savar and Ashulia have been closed under Section 13(1), according to local media reports.The disruption has prompted concern over the impact on an industry that employs more than four million people and accounts for roughly 80% of Bangladesh's export earnings.The timing is particularly sensitive, with factories entering the run-up to Christmas, traditionally one of the busiest periods for garment exports.For an industry already facing pressure over production costs, the combination of unresolved wage demands, factory shutdowns and the risk of losing buyer confidence could make the coming weeks critical.You use AI every day. articles.title: A five-inch pot sat on an elderly couple’s dining-room sideboard, estimated at £500–£800; experts identified it as rare Song dynasty Ru ware, and it sold for £320,000
articles.summary: Discover the astonishing story of an elderly couple's overlooked bowl that was valued at just £500-£800 but sold for £320,000, revealing a rare 900-year-old Song dynasty Ru ware masterpiece. Learn how its identification led to an auction frenzy and shattered records.
articles.body: A lifetime of household possessions can hold stories that even their owners are oblivious to. Some objects sit quietly in a home for decades, blending into the humdrum of everyday surroundings. One such object was a small bowl belonging to an elderly couple in Lincolnshire. Standing just a few inches tall, it had been valued at no more than a few hundred pounds. That changed once experts recognised its rarity and age. According to the BBC, it went under the hammer at Stamford Auction Rooms and three bidders took the price to £320,000.The object was believed to be a previously undocumented example of Ru ware from China’s Song Dynasty. It was treated as one item among the possessions being cleared after the couple’s deaths.A modest estimated value for an elusive treasureThe bowl was around five inches tall and had a green, crackled glaze. Reh’s Galleries described it as a small celadon pot or bowl that stood on the dining-room sideboard. It had been found there during the clearance of the couple’s house, the BBC reported. The item was sent to a local auction house by relatives who had arranged the disposal of the household contents. Initially, Stamford Auction Rooms had placed a modest estimate of £500 to £800 on it, according to the BBC. Jessica Wall, the auctioneer and director of the business, told the BBC that Chinese ceramics were tricky to value.Such uncertainty in visual identification is not unusual; it is well documented. Following a research paper by Thomas Delbey and colleagues titled “Characterising Chinese Ru ware”, genuine Northern Song Ru ware was produced for only about 20 years before the kilns were abandoned. As a result, fewer than 90 documented pieces are left worldwide.After the bowl’s identification, the interest surrounding the lot changed. It was thought to have been made during the Song dynasty, which lasted from 960 to 1279 AD. As per a Lincolnshire Live report in 2021, it was believed to date from the 12th century. Ru ware is associated with a restrained finish rather than elaborate decoration. The BBC described the bowls with a bluish or greenish-grey glaze crossed by a fine network of cracks.A bidding frenzy that broke the house recordInterest gathered before the sale after the Stamford Auction Rooms circulated its photographs and videos, Lincolnshire Live reported. Then, three collectors competed for it at the auction held on 28 August 2021. One bidder was in the room, having travelled from London; another took part online from Italy, while the third bid by telephone. The eventual buyer was the London attendee, whose identity was not divulged.Wall described the bidding as unexpected in her account to Lincolnshire Live. She recalled to the outlet that the price had reached a five-figure sum which she considered a good result. But to her surprise, the numbers continued to rise: "When it got to £10,000, I thought that was good, but it kept going.“When it got to £10,000, I thought that was good, but it kept going. At £140,000, eyebrows were raised, and it eventually got to £320,000 – it was thrilling, really.”The hammer eventually fell at £320,000, but it was not the final amount paid by the buyer. Rehs Galleries reported a total of £385,000, with premium included. Before the bowl appeared, Stamford Auction Rooms’ highest recorded sale had been a 7.5-carat diamond solitaire ring that sold for £78,000 in 2019, as per the Lincolnshire Live report. The Ru ware bowl therefore more than quadrupled the previous house record on its hammer price alone. The sale also brought an unexpected return to the family whose relatives had asked the auction house to value the contents of the home.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Hungary recovers $20 million in cash, some buried or hidden, in probe of ex-minister
articles.summary: BUDAPEST — Hungarian authorities have recovered nearly $20 million in cash, some buried in forests or hidden in farm buildings and warehouses, in a bribery investigation into Miklós Seszták, a minister under former leader ​Viktor Orbán.
articles.body: BUDAPEST — Hungarian authorities have recovered nearly $20 million in cash, some buried in forests or hidden in farm buildings and warehouses, in a bribery investigation into Miklós Seszták, a minister under former leader ​Viktor Orbán. Prime Minister Péter Magyar ousted Orbán after 16 years in power in an April election, pledging ‌to mend ties with the European Union strained by years of disagreements under Orbán, and to launch a sweeping investigation into allegations of graft. The clampdown is part of an anti-graft drive the centre-right Magyar has dubbed “Operation Purgatory”, which 70% of respondents rated as “very important” in a survey by the ​pollster Median carried by news website HVG this week. “During searches, investigators found large amounts of cash buried in forests, ​hidden in farm buildings, warehouses and a residential property, and stored in a high-value safe in ⁠a secluded location,” the National Asset Recovery and Protection Office said late on Friday. Finance Minister András Kármán said it took a ​dozen State Treasury workers eight hours using banknote counters to count the cash that had been retrieved. Magyar said the recovered cash ​signalled the end of what he described as a “mafia” led by Orbán’s right-wing Fidesz party and his Christian Democrat allies during Orbán’s 16-year rule. Fidesz wrote in a Facebook post that it hoped Seszták was not connected to the cash. “Since the change of regime, every lawmaker in Hungary has sworn ​an oath to abide by and enforce the law. Fidesz-KDNP (Christian Democrats) cannot associate itself with anyone who fails to do so. ​We trust that the images published by the NVVH (asset recovery office) have nothing to do with Miklós Seszták,” Fidesz wrote. Seszták — Orbán’s development minister ‌from 2014 ⁠to 2018 — has denied wrongdoing. His lawyer, Gabor Papp, did not respond to a request for comment on the recovery office’s statement. But he told local news website Telex the seized cash did not belong to Seszták, a member of parliament’s Economic and Energy Affairs Committee. He added that the bribery case also involved other suspects. Call to relinquish mandate But Bence Rétvári, parliamentary group leader of the ​Christian Democrats, said Seszták, ⁠the party’s vice chair, should relinquish his parliamentary mandate as he seeks to clear his name. “This is an individual criminal case, and the criminal proceedings must be kept strictly separate from our ​political community,” Rétvári said on Facebook. “Péter Magyar wants to use it to portray the entire right ​as a criminal ⁠organisation. We reject this in the strongest possible terms!” In separate investigations, two former ministers from Orbán’s government and former central bank chief György Matolcsy are under arrest over graft accusations. They have denied wrongdoing. Authorities have also detained Orbán’s brother in a people-smuggling case that ⁠the former ​leader has dismissed as an act of political revenge. Gábor Török, a political scientist, ​said the images of the cash were so vivid they likely spelled doom for Fidesz, whose support fell by half from its pre-election level to 16% ​of voters in November, a Median survey showed.

articles.body: A DNA test intended to explore family ancestry can sometimes reveal far more than expected. The production recently became the setting for another emotional moment when seven of his half-siblings travelled from the United States to Canada and surprised him at a Toronto performance.DNA test revealed an unexpected family historyTomaschoff's discovery began in 2022, when he bought a DNA test kit. After he mentioned the purchase to his mother, his parents told him the next morning that the man who had raised him was not his biological father. Recalling his reaction, Tomaschoff told The Washington Post, "I was profoundly shocked. I had never remotely considered this to be a possibility."He also described the experience of having his understanding of his family changed, saying, "It was like meeting aliens," to The Washington Post. Two months later, the test results revealed that he had at least 15 half-siblings conceived through the same sperm donor. He subsequently identified 20 more, bringing the total to more than 35. The discovery prompted him to investigate his biological origins and establish contact with some of his newly found siblings.The revelation also brought a complicated set of emotions. While the discovery created opportunities to connect with people who shared his background, it required him to reconsider parts of the family story he had previously understood.Turned family secret into a musicalRather than keeping the experience private, Tomaschoff decided to explore it through theatre. He created Our Little Secret, a musical inspired by his DNA discovery and the complicated family relationships that followed.The production combines personal experiences with humour and music to examine themes of identity, parenthood, family secrets and unexpected connections. By presenting the story on stage, Tomaschoff found a way to explore a deeply personal subject while allowing audiences to reflect on the broader questions it raises about family and belonging.The musical was first presented at the Toronto Fringe Festival in 2023 as Our Little Secret: The 23andMe Musical. The production featured Tomaschoff as its creator and performer. The musical later travelled to other cities before returning to Toronto for a larger production at CAA Theatre. According to the show's official website, its November 2026 run was scheduled from November 3 to 22.Tomaschoff's parents were initially uncomfortable with the idea of their long-kept family secret being revealed publicly through the musical. However, they eventually embraced the production. "They came around, and now we feel like this show really represents us as a family," Tomaschoff told The Washington Post.Seven half-siblings surprised him in TorontoThe latest development in Tomaschoff's story came during a Toronto performance when seven of his half-siblings travelled from the United States to surprise him. Their appearance turned an ordinary performance into an unexpected family reunion. The siblings' decision to attend the show also reflected how a discovery made through a DNA test had developed into real relationships and connections across national borders.For Tomaschoff, the reunion brought the story behind the musical into the theatre itself. The people whose shared biological history had inspired the production were now part of the audience, making the experience especially meaningful.A personal discovery became a shared storyTomaschoff's experience highlights how consumer DNA testing can reveal unexpected biological relationships and reshape people's understanding of their families. Such discoveries can bring excitement and opportunities for connection, but they can also raise difficult questions about identity, parenthood and long-kept secrets.Through Our Little Secret, Tomaschoff has turned his personal experience into a theatrical production that allows audiences to engage with these questions. The surprise appearance of seven half-siblings at his Toronto show added another chapter to a story that began with a DNA test and developed into an expanding family connection.You use AI every day. articles.title: Italy fines Meta $880m over photo privacy
articles.summary: Regulator said Meta’s ‘lack of cooperation’ and the large number of people affected contributed to size of the fine.
articles.body:
Italian regulators have fined Meta 805 million euros ($887m) for accessing users’ photos without their consent.

The Facebook app on Android devices “accessed photos, videos and associated metadata stored on Italian users’ smartphones without specific consent and without informing them”, Garante, the Italian data privacy authority, said Saturday.

The issue relates specifically to the “Get suggestions from gallery when browsing Facebook” feature, which suggests photos and videos from the phone’s gallery for posting while browsing.

This feature violates the Italian law implementing the EU’s ePrivacy directive, the authority said.

Garante said the app’s process for collecting consent is too generic and does not allow users to fully understand the specific permissions they are allowing by accepting. The suggestions option was also enabled by default.

The figure of 805 million euros is by far the largest fine ever imposed by the Italian regulator.

Garante said Meta must fix the unclear consent notification and disable it being set by default, suggesting that roughly 20 million Italian Android users could have been affected by it.

The regulator also highlighted a “lack of cooperation” by Meta and said an earlier violation, which resulted in a 2019 fine, was a contributing factor in their decision.

The amount is roughly 0.47 percent of Meta’s global turnover.

The proceedings did not address the possible use of content to train artificial intelligence, which Meta denies.

Meta has not yet publicly commented on the matter, and it has the right to appeal the regulator’s decision.
